newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong 1996 net in line, 1997 seen better.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong 1996 net in line, 1997 seen better.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd's 1996 results came in much as the market expected on Wednesday, boosted by an exceptional gain, and analysts said more property sales and exceptionals should fuel a better 1997 performance.
The Hong Kong property developer posted a 23.7 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$13.77 billion (US$1.78 billion).
The bottom line figure included a gain of HK$1.51 billion from the listing of Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) in July and the placement of CKI shares.
"It's a good set of results with no major surprises," said David Low, research manager at Asia Equity. "Essentially it is going to be a very good year from there."
Low had predicted 1996 net profit growth of 20 percent.
"Underlying growth was 10 percent. It is still very good considering the fact that they had not been selling many projects last year," he said.
After a slow year for property sales in 1996, analysts said Cheung Kong should see a pick up in property profits in 1997.
"The major boost to its earnings is still property sales which should be very strong," said Vickers Ballas property analyst Desmond Cheung.
Cheung Kong said it expected to release several residential projects for sale in 1997, including The Green Wood at Laguna Verde and Maywood Court at Kingswood Villas.
"These will bring in considerable cash income to the group," it said.
Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities, said the two residential property developments alone should contribute profit of more than HK$6.0 billion to Cheung Kong.
Chairman Li Ka-shing said Cheung Kong would also book the remaining HK$7.7 billion from the CKI placement and flotation "this year and beyond".
"The company's bottom line has been well protected by an exceptional item arising from the disposal of Cheung Kong Infrastructure," said Chan.

"Basically they are already sitting on a very comfortable bottom line for the prospective year and in fact for the coming year Cheung Kong will only focus on the sale of two major development projects," he said.
Chan said including an exceptional item related to the CKI disposal, he expected net profit growth of 51 percent in 1997 to about HK$20.8 billion.
Low expected full-year profit of about HK$24 billion, 50 percent coming from Cheung Kong's 48.9-percent-owned Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and 40 percent from property development.

Analysts said aggressive bidding at a government land auction on Tuesday and the record price of HK$11.82 billion paid by Sino Land Co Ltd for a 25,592 square metre site in Chai Wan demonstrated that property developers would be able to raise prices for property sales.
"They should capture the market and capitalise on that by raising prices," said Low, adding that Cheung Kong had already raised prices at its Laguna Verde development by 10 percent.

Cheung Kong said on Tuesday it had raised prices for an additional 72 units at its Kingswood Villa development to HK$4,212 per square foot compared with HK$4,089 per square foot asked for an initial 48 units offered at the project.
"The value of its property exposure will increasingly be recognised," said Low.
Chan said he had a buy rating on the stock and saw it reaching HK$82 in 12 months. Cheung Kong shares ended on a gain of HK$0.50 on Wednesday at HK$70.50.
